result.title: When Do Learned Blocks Preserve Causal Meaning? Block Identifiability and Constructive Causal Abstractions
result.summary: Standard identifiability theory assumes one-dimensional latent factors, but learned representations can encode latent information across multidimensional blocks whose internal coordinates are not uniquely determined. When such blocks are used to represent and intervene on higher-level concepts, it is unclear whether their causal meaning survives the transformations left unresolved by block-identifiability. We connect block-identifiability to constructive causal abstraction. We show that block-diagonal invertible transformations followed by compatible coordinate permutations form the maximal class that preserves every constructive causal abstraction built on those blocks. This guarantee assumes that the correspondence between blocks and concepts is updated with the representation. A small synthetic experiment with additive autoencoders shows that high-level interventions can be transferred between independently learned representations while approximately preserving their intended effects.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「块可辨识性」与构造性因果抽象联系起来，证明块对角可逆变换加兼容坐标置换构成保留此类因果抽象的最大变换类，并用加性自编码器的合成实验说明高层干预可在独立学得的表示间近似迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 关心的「内部状态是否保留任务必要信息及其因果作用」可能相关：其最大变换类结论可供核查 latent 表示在坐标变换下因果意义保持的边界，但该工作面向一般表示学习理论，与视觉多模态推理尚无直接联系。
